sources.quote: Alberta has run a provincial Rat Control Program since 1950 and has kept the province effectively free of breeding rat populations
sources.title: Alberta's Rat Control Program | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: The province has had no breeding populations of rats for over 70 years thanks to its storied Rat Control Program. Since the early 1950s, Alberta has maintained a Rat Control Zone (RCZ) along the eastern border with Saskatchewan. A dedicated email address to report rat sightings and a live cam are tools the team has added to a program that has been around since 1950.

sources.quote: Section 6 prohibits advertising that is likely to create an erroneous impression about a product's safety or registration
sources.publisher: Department of Justice Canada (Justice Laws Website)
sources.title: Pest Control Products Act - Justice Laws Website
sources.evidence: Section 6(7): No person shall package, label or advertise a pest control product in a way that is false, misleading or likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character, value, quantity, composition, safety or registration.

sources.quote: The Pesticides Act and O. Reg. 63/09 require an operator licence for the business and a technician licence for supervised staff
sources.title: Pesticide licences and permits | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: Unless exempt, you or your business require a pesticide operator licence if you operate a pesticide extermination business in Ontario or employ people who apply pesticides commercially. Unless exempt, you need a pesticide exterminator licence to apply pesticides commercially on any property that you or your employer do not own or farm. Licensed exterminators work with technicians and trainees who can use most Class C and D pesticides.

sources.quote: exempts health and safety uses such as stinging insects and ticks, so wasp work is legal to advertise
sources.title: Technical guidance: Pesticides Act and Ontario Regulation 63/09 – landscape licensed exterminators | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: For health and safety purposes, pesticides can be used if they have a use related to the destruction, prevention or control of animals that bite, sting, are venomous or carry disease. Licensed structural exterminators can control animals that bite, sting, are venomous or carry disease on land (such as controlling ticks on a lawn).

sources.quote: BC's Integrated Pest Management Act requires a pesticide user licence and structural applicator certificates
sources.title: Authorization to sell or use pesticides - Province of British Columbia
sources.evidence: There are 4 types of authorizations under the Integrated Pest Management Act and the Integrated Pest Management Regulation: Certificates are issued to individual pesticide applicators, and licenses are available for businesses that have certified pesticide applicators. Structural pest control certification is used to manage pests (including insects, rodents and birds) invading or damaging structures where the applicator is working on a fee-for-service basis.

sources.quote: Extermination firms hold a Class C, subclass C5 permit under the provincial pesticide regime and technicians hold CD5 certificates
sources.title: Pesticide application on green spaces, golf courses, indoor plants and for pest management | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: Companies that apply pesticides for pest management purposes must hold a permit Application in pest management (subcategory C5 or D5), and individuals applying pesticides for these purposes must hold a certificate for application in pest management (subcategory CD5) or work under the supervision of the certificate holder.

sources.quote: As a general rule the landlord does, through the section 20 maintenance duty in Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act
sources.title: LTB Brochure - Maintenance and Repairs
sources.evidence: Section 20 of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 states that a landlord is responsible for providing and maintaining a residential complex, including the rental units in it, in a good state of repair and fit for habitation and for complying with health, safety, housing and maintenance standards. A landlord must also take steps to control pests such as cockroaches and mice.

sources.quote: Public Health Agency of Canada surveillance shows blacklegged tick range expanding and reported Lyme cases climbing steeply
sources.title: Surveillance for Lyme disease in Canada, 2009 to 2019, CCDR 48(5) - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Incidence of reported cases has increased more than 17-fold from 2009 through 2019. During 2009–2019, a total of 10,150 LD cases were reported by the provinces to the Public Health Agency of Canada. This occurred in part due to changes in climate, which has contributed to increases in the abundance and geographic range of blacklegged tick populations in central and eastern Canada.

sources.quote: Google folded the Guaranteed and Screened badges into a single Google Verified badge in October 2025 and retired the money back guarantee behind the old one
sources.title: About Google Verified badge - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Local Services Ads will be simplifying badging by launching a single, more cohesive Google Verified badge for all advertisers effective October 20, 2025. Google will discontinue all existing Local Services Ads badges, including Google Guaranteed, Google Screened, and License Verified by Google, effective October 20, 2025. The Money Back Guarantee associated with the Google Guarantee badge will also be discontinued.

sources.quote: pest control is a supported home service category in Canada, and you pay per lead rather than per click once Google has screened licence and insurance
sources.title: Getting started with Local Services Ads - Canada - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: In Canada, Google Local Services Ads are available for the following service categories: Junk removal services, Lawn care services, Locksmiths, Removals, Pest control services, Plumbers, Roofers, Tree services, Water damage services, Window cleaning services, and Window repair services. Businesses seeking to advertise with Local Services Ads are required to complete appropriate background checks and have appropriate licenses and insurance, as applicable.
